requirements.evidence: Migrations match the schema contract incl. named indexes and the stored generated owner_seq + unique (entity_id, owner_seq) (create_entity_memberships_table.php:16-29). Policies (EntityPolicy.php, EntityMembershipPolicy.php) implement every rule, incl. owner-never-deleted, self-removal and last-manager. EntityController::pick authorizes before writing the session and logs on 'audit'. Members: exists:users,email, duplicate -> error on email, Rule::enum(...)->only(UserRole::manageable()) on role. Settings: locked entity, unique-ignore slug, delete clears session, transfer restricted to admins of this entity other than caller, abort 403 when owner missing. Dashboard owner notice and settings link guarded by @can. Gap: Settings.php:88-99 takes lockForUpdate() outside the DB::transaction, so the reads that decide the transfer are not part of the atomic unit (locks are released immediately in autocommit).

conventions.evidence: Policies used everywhere ($this->authorize, @can), $fillable via #[Fillable], Blade component x-entity-nav, Bulma markup, lang keys in both locales, CHANGELOG and docs/database-schema.md updated. Deviations: domain writes (add member, assign role, remove member, save/delete/transfer) are done inline in Livewire components instead of app/Actions/* classes; Livewire validation uses inline $this->validate([...]) / validator() rather than the project's #[Validate] attribute pattern (Members.php:40, Settings.php:40); migration names 2026_10_29_000000/000001 look hand-written rather than generated.

security.evidence: Every public action re-authorizes server-side (Members.php:38,68,91; Settings.php:39,67-68,86); entity is #[Locked] in all three components; action IDs are resolved via $this->entity->memberships()->findOrFail() (Members.php:129-132) and the transfer target via ->admin()->whereKey() scoped to the entity; all output uses {{ }}. Minor: lockForUpdate outside a transaction gives no real protection against a concurrent transfer/role change; public $status is client-writable (escaped, harmless).

tests.evidence: Six feature test files cover data model/indexes (EntityDataModelTest), policies (EntityPoliciesTest), pick incl. 403 with untouched session and audit log (EntityPickTest), pages incl. owner notice and absence of settings URL for non-owners (EntityPagesTest), members incl. unauthorized add/assign/remove, owner-role validation, cross-entity membership tamper (EntityMembersTest:121), settings incl. locked-entity tamper ('Cannot update locked property'), demoted-owner calls, transfer to employee/foreign/self/null -> 403, string id from select.

simplicity.evidence: Lean policies with a small hasRole/isManager helper; reuses existing x-form-field/x-button components. Minor duplication: Dashboard::render recomputes ownership with owner()->where('user_id', ...) while the view already uses @can('manageSettings'); session-clearing logic is repeated in Members::removeMember and Settings::delete.

readability.evidence: Clear names (membershipOf, isLastManager), short methods, useful comments explaining why (Settings.php:102 'Demote before promoting...', Members.php:126 docblock), consistent with sibling style; no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: All files serve the task: models, migrations, factories, policies, controller, three Livewire pages, views, lang keys, routes, docs, changelog and tests. No onboarding, switcher, middleware or navbar work; audit logging on member actions is a small, related addition.

issues.explanation: Domain writes (add/assign/remove member, update/delete entity, transfer ownership) are implemented inside Livewire components instead of app/Actions/* use-case classes as the conventions require.

lockForUpdate() reads for the owner and target are executed before DB::transaction starts, so the locks are released immediately and the check-then-write of the transfer is not atomic under concurrency.
Validation uses inline rule arrays passed to $this->validate() rather than the project's #[Validate] attribute pattern on the public properties.
Sequential 000000/000001 timestamps suggest the migrations were hand-named rather than created with make:migration.
isOwner is recomputed with a separate query although the view already relies on @can('manageSettings'), which expresses the same check.
public ?string $status is client-writable; harmless since it is escaped, but a flash/protected value would be cleaner.

review.summary: The change implements the entities/memberships data model with a portable one-owner constraint, policies, entity pick, and the dashboard/members/settings Livewire pages with thorough server-side authorization, locked entity binding and extensive tests including unauthorized and tamper cases. It would be approvable with small fixes, but domain writes bypass the project's Actions convention, validation does not use #[Validate], and the transfer's row locks are taken outside the transaction.
